title: Two pianos, one submerged cathedral
work: La cathédrale engloutie, Préludes I, No. 10
question: How do Meyer and Ilić distribute time between the opening fifths, the broad chords and their quiet echo?
intro: Marcelle Meyer recorded this prelude at Salle Adyar, Paris, on 15 February 1956; Ivan Ilić recorded it in Paris in April 2006. Both play the solo-piano work, whose broad chordal melody returns later as a quiet, lower echo. The automatic alignment covers 0–330 seconds of Meyer against 0–310 seconds of Ilić, excluding the final decay; it remains provisional, not a score alignment. Meyer’s recording is used under the documented European recording-rights expiry claim, not an assertion of US public-domain status.

passages.note: Follow the chord tops as a melody; compare phrase lengths without comparing the transfers’ playback levels.

passages.label: Quiet echo
passages.note: The lower, quieter return offers a second hearing of the chordal tune: compare its pacing with the first statement.
